column1: # clues.tsv for ft_is_prime — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".

Where does the very definition of a prime start? Below which integer can a number never qualify, and which two small numbers are the first that do? Decide what happens before you ever enter a divisor loop.

To know a number has no divisor, how far up do you really have to search? If a factor existed above a certain point, its partner would already have appeared below it — what is that turning point? Test it on perfect squares of small numbers.

For very large inputs the loop bound itself can betray you. If you compare a divisor's square against nb, what happens to that product before the comparison even runs? Can you phrase the same limit without ever forming that product?
